answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable token before it may submit jobs or vote on disputes. Rewards accrue to the locked stake, while proven fraud triggers slashing: the protocol destroys part of the deposit and can exclude the identity. Creating a hundred identities then requires a hundred deposits, not just a script; splitting stake among them also dilutes each one’s influence. A lagoon marketplace may reach a summit of activity, but hollow identities still impose a real capital cost on their owner.
